about: Educational source-linked immune-pathway crosswalk. A native bacterial ligand, a synthetic agonist, a microbial delivery platform and a recombinant host cytokine are not interchangeable. Clinical adverse-event attribution is product-specific.

entries.engineered: Engineered bacteria may alter or display immunostimulatory lipoproteins; evidence and safety are strain-, formulation-, and expression-context-specific. Do not infer clinical success from receptor engagement.
entries.synthetic: Synthetic triacylated-lipopeptide mimics, including Amplivant conjugates.
entries.signal: Primarily MyD88-dependent NF-κB / inflammatory pathways; TLR2 pairs with TLR1 for triacylated ligands.
entries.safety: Excess inflammatory stimulation, fever and local reactogenicity; read product-level clinical safety.

entries.natural: TLR3 is classically associated with viral dsRNA; bacterial RNA involvement is context-dependent and not a universal native bacterial TLR3 ligand.
entries.engineered: Research may explore delivery of dsRNA or RNA-like immunostimulatory payloads via microbial systems. Direct clinical safety and receptor-specific attribution have not been established for bacteria-engineered TLR3 agonist delivery.
entries.synthetic: Poly(I:C), poly-ICLC (Hiltonol), BO-112 and rintatolimod (Ampligen); different sensor specificity.
entries.signal: TRIF–TBK1–IRF3 and NF-κB; poly(I:C) can also engage MDA5 and other RNA sensors.
entries.safety: Potential flu-like symptoms, thrombocytopenia, inflammatory toxicity and regimen-specific serious events; use individual studies.

entries.ligand: Gram-negative bacterial LPS / lipid A; monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL)
entries.natural: A well-established receptor for bacterial LPS through the TLR4–MD2 complex; lipid A chemistry strongly affects activity. Indaptus Decoy10 research documented TLR2/4/8/9 agonist activity, but did not establish TLR1/2 versus TLR2/6 pairing.
entries.engineered: Bacteria may be modified to alter their LPS/lipid A immune-stimulation profile. Such changes require product-specific inflammatory safety evaluation and should not be assumed clinically safe.
entries.engineer_level: Established research platform, clinical relevance formulation-specific
entries.synthetic: MPL and synthetic lipid A analogues used in vaccine adjuvant research; SHINGRIX contains bacterial-derived MPL.
entries.signal: TLR4 activates both MyD88 and TRIF pathways, potentially inflammatory cytokines and type I interferon responses.
entries.safety: Local/systemic reactogenicity and potentially excessive inflammatory signaling; whole-vaccine and whole-bacteria safety are distinct.

sources.label: Indaptus killed E. coli receptor profile (TLR2/4/8/9, NOD2, STING)

entries.ligand: Single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) and certain synthetic small-molecule agonists
entries.natural: TLR7 is an endosomal RNA sensor; some bacterial RNAs may activate related RNA sensing systems under specific delivery conditions.
entries.engineered: Bacterial production or delivery of RNA-derived immune cues is an experimental delivery concept. It is not equivalent to approved TLR7 small-molecule agonist therapy.
entries.signal: MyD88–IRF7 and NF-κB; can induce type I interferons, including IFN-α.
entries.safety: Flu-like inflammatory effects and adverse events depend on dose, route and co-therapies.

entries.ligand: Bacterial CpG-rich DNA, and synthetic CpG oligodeoxynucleotides
entries.natural: Bacterial DNA with immunostimulatory CpG motifs is a canonical microbial TLR9 signal; cellular localization determines access.
entries.engineered: Bacterial systems can be investigated as sources or carriers of immunostimulatory DNA; altered nucleic-acid presentation does not imply clinical benefit or component-specific safety.
entries.engineer_level: Bacterial CpG is native; engineered delivery clinical evidence limited
entries.synthetic: CpG 1018 adjuvant in HEPLISAV-B, and research CpG oligonucleotides.
entries.signal: MyD88-mediated pathways and plasmacytoid dendritic-cell IFN-α responses, varying by CpG class.
entries.safety: Vaccine-level serious events/deaths must be distinguished from CpG-adjuvant causality.

entries.ligand: Host cytokine; type I interferon (not a TLR agonist)
entries.natural: Host immune cells produce IFN-α after certain innate sensing events, including some TLR responses. It is not naturally a bacterial TLR ligand.
entries.engineered: Interferon proteins can be manufactured using recombinant expression systems. Engineering live bacteria to deliver bioactive IFN-α in vivo is a separate research question and cannot be assumed clinically validated.
entries.engineer_level: Biomanufacture established; live bacterial delivery not clinically established here
entries.synthetic: PEGASYS (peginterferon alfa-2a) is an exogenous interferon therapy.
entries.safety: Interferon-alfa drugs carry potentially fatal neuropsychiatric, autoimmune, ischemic and infectious risk warnings.

entries.ligand: Host cytokine; type I interferon (not a TLR agonist)
entries.natural: IFN-β is produced by host cells downstream of innate immune sensors such as TLR3/TRIF; bacteria are not its natural cellular source.
entries.engineered: Recombinant protein manufacture and experimental microbial cytokine-delivery concepts are distinct. No live-bacteria-delivered IFN-β human efficacy/safety claim is made here.
entries.engineer_level: Biomanufacture established; live bacterial delivery investigational
entries.synthetic: AVONEX (interferon beta-1a) as a clinically administered interferon product.
entries.safety: Interferon-beta labels warn of psychiatric, hepatic and hematologic adverse events and other severe complications.

sources.label: Type I IFN via bacterial sensing

entries.ligand: Host cytokine; type II interferon (not a TLR agonist)
entries.natural: IFN-γ is produced mainly by activated T and NK cells; it is not a naturally occurring bacterial TLR agonist.
entries.engineered: Engineered probiotic bacteria have delivered IFN-γ locally in published mouse tumor models, including work paired with anti-PD-1. This is preclinical and distinct from recombinant systemic treatment.
entries.engineer_level: Demonstrated in preclinical animal models; not clinical proof
entries.synthetic: ACTIMMUNE (interferon gamma-1b) is a licensed recombinant host-cytokine therapy for specified noncancer indications.
entries.signal: IFNGR1/IFNGR2 → JAK1/JAK2 → STAT1; influences antigen presentation and immunity.
entries.safety: Systemic IFN-γ can have dose-limiting inflammatory effects; live bacterial delivery additionally needs shedding, biodistribution, containment and product-specific risk assessment.
